hook: A single-frame monochrome still image captured by a U.S. military sensor system in 2025, submitted by the FBI to AARO, showing an unidentified dark irregular-shaped object positioned just above a targeting reticle crosshair — with an operator-confirmed inability to identify it.
why_it_matters: This document represents one of the rare instances of FBI-sourced imagery formally submitted through AARO's reporting pipeline, indicating institutional cross-agency cooperation in UAP documentation. The fact that the imagery was redacted before submission — and that no accompanying mission report was provided — limits analytical value but also suggests the underlying collection platform is considered sensitive. The operator's explicit inability to positively identify the object elevates it above noise: this is not a case of resolved ambiguity.
key_findings: The image was captured by a U.S. military sensor system, not a civilian or commercial platform, indicating the UAP was observed within a military operational context in the Western United States.

The FBI submitted the imagery to AARO after applying redactions to the original, meaning the version in the public record is already a second-order product — the full unredacted image remains withheld.
No mission report accompanied the submission, leaving the operational context (flight profile, mission type, sensor mode) entirely undocumented in the public record.
The embedded timestamp in the image is known to be incorrect due to an unconfigured system clock, complicating any attempt to correlate this event with other sensor data or reports.

The object appears as a single dark irregular shape just above the center of a targeting reticle in a grainy monochrome frame — consistent with imagery from infrared or low-light electro-optical military sensors.

legacy_program_connections.reasoning: The document was formally submitted by the FBI directly to AARO as part of its UAP reporting mandate, making AARO the primary institutional recipient and record-holder.
The image originates from a U.S. military sensor system, and Wright-Patterson has historically been the hub for military photographic and sensor analysis related to unidentified aerial phenomena.
The PURSUE release through which this image was disclosed is the product of congressional mandates for UAP transparency, placing this record within that legislative accountability framework.
